judgements.justification: B's AC set the Spotlight from personal enthusiasm ('I personally find ... elegant') on scores 7, 6, 7 with no reviewer above 7.
Neither recommendation rests on a forecast of impact beyond the paper's setting; XqTW's 'paradigm shift' praises the framing.
The response moved scores in both committees (PoYC to 7 in A; XqTW and qDh3 in B), so A's scores were not left unchanged.
B's bohc gave a 7 on four generic lines with no weakness and no discussion; A's omcp also wrote a short review and kept a 5 without a reason.
Only A asked for FGSM/PGD baselines at comparable eps and a cross-entropy ablation (plus the AC's DeepFool), and A's meta-review rests on it.
UycQ (A) and qDh3, XqTW (B) all saw ACE as a small-eps FGSM-style attack; B held problem novelty enough, A held technical depth as the bar.
Every score change followed the authors' response, not reviewer discussion.
No rating clearly contradicts its own text; omcp's 5 matches its two stated cons.
All six reviewers gave confidence 4; none deferred to a borderline score for lack of expertise.
A's AC followed UycQ, who was one of two 5s, not an outlier; B's AC followed no single reviewer.
UycQ and qDh3 wrote similar critiques but differed in what they weighted after the rebuttal, not in scale calibration.
B's meta-review cites 'very well received' and 'consensus in accepting' for a Spotlight though no reviewer exceeded 7, while A's 5, 5, 7 spread held it at reject.
The new AdvProp and cross-architecture results went to both committees and were run by the authors; A's PoYC saw them too.
B's meta-review says the main concerns were addressed and omits qDh3's open requests and the shared point that the method is a simple FGSM-style attack.
omcp's con that no experiment supports harm to popular uncertainty methods is wrong (Sections 5.1-5.4), and omcp kept the 5 that helped sink A.
No concession about the results went unpunished; XqTW raised after the label-proxy argument, not after an unfavourable result.
A's AC raised a DeepFool baseline in the meta-review that no reviewer had asked for, so the authors never answered it and it stood in A's reject.
The scores differ (5, 5, 7 against 7, 6, 7), so the split is not a tier threshold on near-identical reviews.
All reviewers had confidence 4; A's AC followed the majority and no better-informed verdict was passed over.
B's requests (lending scenario, AdvProp, variance) were closable by new results, while UycQ's core objection, that ACE is a rescaled FGSM/PGD, no response could remove.
PoYC's 7 is A's outlier but did not set the tier; A's other scores (5, 5) do not match B's.
No outlying reviewer ignored the response; omcp, who replied only briefly, was not the outlier, and bohc's 7 matched B.
No area chair discarded a detractor while defending acceptance.
Neither committee raised audience breadth or venue fit.
A's meta-review says omcp 'supported the concern' and 'all reviewers' agree on more evaluations; the record shows PoYC raising to 7 and omcp giving no reason.
Most reviewers in both committees replied to the response.
No reviewer said they could not verify the results; all had confidence 4.
A split two to one, not evenly.
The notes record the same lending scenario and AdvProp results given to both committees.
No novelty verdict rested on a wrong account of prior work; the FGSM comparison is correct.
B's Spotlight has a stated ground, the AC's own enthusiasm, which R01 covers.
No reviewer contested the framing from a neighbouring field's premises.
Both committees had engaged positive reviewers (PoYC in A, XqTW in B), and none rated well above the accept level.
No one rejected the paper because promised revisions were too large.
Neither AC relied on input outside the record.

reasoning: The accept/reject split is mainly a weighting difference (R06): both committees saw ACE as a simple FGSM-style attack, B judged problem novelty enough and A did not. The rebuttal could answer B's requests but not A's core objection (R20), A alone asked for baseline attacks (R05), and A kept an inattentive detractor score built partly on a misread (R04, R15) that its meta-review misreported as support (R25). A's AC added an unanswerable DeepFool demand (R17). The Spotlight tier comes from B's AC's own enthusiasm and a one-sided 'well received' meta-review (R01, R12, R14). The stage 1 candidates all map to existing reasons, so none was added.
